email.subject: Re: Reaction delivery ruling, from 13 October
email.body:
Tanya, today, in the delivery routing ruling, you said: "we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four" [^1]. In the same memory, Tina pushed back on the batching window, and you held: the bundle closes when the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather than sending on its own. [^2] The per-skill alternative, with client-side collapsing, was considered and set aside. [^3]

So now, reactions go into one bundle per run for each person. [^1] The bundle closes with the run, and anything that misses the close goes into the next run's bundle. [^2] Per-skill delivery is not the route. [^3]

My read is that the reaction-delivery note, which has each skill sending as it finishes, no longer describes the system, so it needs rewriting. *(uncommitted)* That suggests to me that a late reaction now reaches the reader a run later than it would have, *(uncommitted)* and that no client-side collapsing has to be built, since the ordering stays on our side. [^3] If that holds, the per-skill notes are the first thing to revisit.

Does a reaction that waits a full run still earn its place for the person who needs it today? Does the decision-capture-at-consensus framing still hold for reactions that arrive a run late? Is there any skill that still has to send on its own, outside the bundle?
